_comment: Candidate passages for the food-after-60 belief. Each must be checked word for word against the official PDF (nin.res.in) before human_verified is set to true and 'checked' says how. Page numbers: PDF page / printed page number, from a text extraction; confirm them while checking.

passages.quote: for healthy older people, the diet should provide at least 1.0–1.2 g protein/kg body weight/day

passages.source_name: ICMR–National Institute of Nutrition, Dietary Guidelines for Indians 2024 (Guideline 16)
passages.quote: As age advances people become less active, their metabolism slows, and their energy requirement decreases.

passages.source_name: ICMR–National Institute of Nutrition, Dietary Guidelines for Indians 2024 (Guideline 16)
passages.quote: An elderly person needs fewer calories but more micronutrients than someone in mid-life.
passages._where: Guideline 16, 'What are the reasons for special nutritional needs for the elderly?', PDF p.117 (printed p.100)

passages.source_name: ICMR–National Institute of Nutrition, Dietary Guidelines for Indians 2024 (Guideline 16)
passages.quote: The body of an ageing adult undergoes multiple physiological changes such as impaired digestion, and protein utilization, altered body composition, insulin resistance, inflammation and decreased bone density.
passages._where: Guideline 16, same section, PDF p.117 (printed p.100)

passages.source_name: ICMR–National Institute of Nutrition, Dietary Guidelines for Indians 2024 (Guideline 16)
passages.quote: It is recommended to consume well cooked, soft food preparations with less salt and moderate amounts of spices
passages._where: Guideline 16, 'What type of diet should the elderly consume?', PDF p.118 (printed p.101)

passages.source_name: ICMR–National Institute of Nutrition, Dietary Guidelines for Indians 2024 (Guideline 16)
passages.quote: Minimizing or avoiding highly or ultra-processed and HFSS foods will delay age-related diseases.
passages._where: Guideline 16, same section, PDF p.118 (printed p.101). HFSS = high fat, sugar, salt

passages.source_name: ICMR–National Institute of Nutrition, Dietary Guidelines for Indians 2024 (Guideline 16, Figure 16.1)
passages.quote: One may consume sugar, but it must be restricted to 25–30 grams per day.
passages._where: Note under Figure 16.1, suggested diet for elderly men (>60 yrs), PDF p.120 (printed p.103)

passages.source_name: ICMR–National Institute of Nutrition, Dietary Guidelines for Indians 2024 (Guideline 11)
passages.quote: There is a strong association between salt intake and blood pressure.
passages._where: Guideline 11, 'What are the health problems associated with excessive salt/sodium intake?', PDF p.91 (printed p.74)

passages.source_name: ICMR–National Institute of Nutrition, Dietary Guidelines for Indians 2024 (Guideline 11)
passages.quote: Salt intake in our population generally exceeds the requirement. It should not be more than 5g per day.
passages._where: Guideline 11, same section, PDF p.91 (printed p.74)
